outroLine: Match the identities exactly — then prove the route.

beats.shot: Land on the supplier's Delivery tab (HTTP selected). Cursor touches the protocol rail, opens Output format and picks cXML — the network-credentials block reveals.
beats.vo: cXML is the format supplier networks like Coupa, Ariba and Jaggaer speak. On this supplier's Delivery tab, pick cXML as the output format — and every order for this supplier is converted to cXML right before it's sent.

beats.shot: Cursor rests on the 'cXML network credentials' block and traces the three party rows — From, To, Sender — each a domain + identity pair.
beats.vo: cXML proves who you are with three party identities in the message header — From, To, and Sender. Each one is a domain, which names the identifier scheme, and an identity, the value inside it.

beats.shot: Cursor fills From domain (DUNS) + From identity, then To domain (NetworkId) + To identity. Obviously-sample values only.
beats.vo: From is usually you, the buyer. To is the supplier, or their network. The supplier gives you these exact values — an identity with its matching domain. A mismatched domain is the most common reason an endpoint rejects the credential, so copy both exactly as issued.

beats.shot: Cursor fills Sender domain + identity, then types into 'Sender shared secret' (placeholder: Optional — supplier-issued shared secret).
beats.vo: Sender is the party that authenticates the connection — often the same as From — and it carries the shared secret the network issued you. That secret is write-only. Once saved, it's encrypted and never shown back — and when you edit later, leaving it blank keeps the stored one.

beats.shot: Cursor moves to the footer Test-fire button and rests on it (dimmed until the setup is saved; never clicked — no mock backend).
beats.vo: Once the setup is saved, test-fire it. ProcuLink posts a real test payload to the endpoint and shows you the exact result it got back.

beats.shot: Cursor rests on the green 'How sending works' card — the honest endpoint-answered-is-not-acceptance framing.
beats.vo: And be precise about what a green result means. The endpoint answered — that is not the same as the supplier accepting the order. A cXML network returns its own acceptance status, and an order can still be rejected downstream. ProcuLink never pretends otherwise.
